subsystems.name: Antenna array
subsystems.role: collects the radiation; the number and spacing of dishes set the resolution and sensitivity.
parts: 54 dishes of 12 m diameter plus 12 of 7 m in a compact sub-array
precision reflector panels and backing structure

subsystems.name: Receiver front ends
subsystems.role: amplify and down-convert faint millimetre waves with very low noise.
parts: receiver cartridges covering bands from about 35 GHz to 950 GHz

subsystems.name: Cryogenics
subsystems.role: holds the mixers near 4 K so their own thermal noise does not swamp the sky signal.

subsystems.name: Frequency reference and local oscillator
subsystems.role: gives every antenna the same phase and frequency, which is what makes the array act as one telescope.

subsystems.name: Correlator and computing
subsystems.role: digitises the signals and multiplies every antenna pair to form visibilities.

subsystems.name: Calibration and imaging
subsystems.role: turns raw visibilities into cubes of molecular line emission.
parts: interferometric imaging and spectral-line analysis software

buildSteps.title: Pick and build the site
buildSteps.detail: The array sits at roughly 5,000 m on the Chajnantor plateau in northern Chile, where the air is thin and extremely dry — water vapour absorbs exactly the wavelengths being observed. Roads, power, fibre links and oxygen-equipped facilities must be built at that altitude.

buildSteps.title: Make the dishes
buildSteps.detail: Each antenna's reflector is assembled from many panels on a stiff backing structure, with surface errors held to tens of micrometres so that short millimetre waves stay in focus.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the receiver cartridges
buildSteps.detail: Niobium SIS junctions are made in a cleanroom by depositing and patterning superconducting and insulating layers a few nanometres thick, then mounted in waveguide blocks machined to micron tolerances.

buildSteps.title: Cool and integrate the receivers
buildSteps.detail: Each cartridge goes into a vacuum dewar cooled by a helium cryocooler, wired to low-noise amplifiers and a local-oscillator feed before being slid into the antenna cabin.

buildSteps.title: Distribute the reference signal
buildSteps.detail: A central hydrogen maser and photonic link system delivers a phase-stable tone to every antenna, so all 66 stations stay coherent with each other.

buildSteps.title: Digitise and correlate
buildSteps.detail: Signals are sampled at billions of samples per second, shipped over optical fibre to the correlator building, and cross-multiplied in every antenna pairing across the observing band.

buildSteps.title: Move antennas to change resolution
buildSteps.detail: A purpose-built transporter lifts a 100-tonne antenna and carries it along the plateau tracks, so the array can be spread from a few hundred metres to 16 km to trade surface brightness sensitivity for sharpness.

buildSteps.title: Commission and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: New bands are proven on bright quasars, planets and known molecular lines before science use, and every observation is calibrated for atmosphere, bandpass and phase.

prerequisites.why: no ordinary amplifier is quiet enough at these frequencies; the SIS junction's near-quantum-limited noise is what makes weak molecular lines detectable.
without it the receiver's own noise would exceed the astronomical signal.
interferometry only works if each antenna's phase can be compared with the others to a fraction of a wavelength.
correlating dozens of antennas over gigahertz-wide bands is a large computing problem, not an analogue one.
atmospheric water vapour blocks the submillimetre windows that carry the most interesting lines.
sparse arrays sample the sky incompletely and require deconvolution to recover an image.

pathway.milestone: routine spectral-line imaging of planet-forming disks at sub-astronomical-unit scales
pathway.unlocks: maps of snowlines, rings and organic inventories in the exact regions where planets form.

pathway.milestone: full deployment of the lowest-frequency receiver band and the Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade
pathway.unlocks: much wider instantaneous bandwidth, so many more molecular lines are captured in a single observation and surveys become far faster.

pathway.milestone: joint campaigns with infrared and optical facilities, plus next-generation centimetre arrays
pathway.unlocks: matching disk gas, dust and ice measurements to what is later seen in exoplanet atmospheres.

pathway.milestone: a continuous chemical accounting from cold interstellar cloud to disk to planet
pathway.unlocks: a physical basis for saying which volatiles, including water, arrive on habitable worlds and where they came from.
